messages.content: You are a behavior neutralizer. Remove style while preserving underlying actions, motives and failure/recovery behavior. Return JSON.

Convert each response into a neutral behavior-only summary.

Scenario:
A mechanism you previously agreed not to disturb; then investigating the anomaly may delay work that already functions. Finishing the routine is satisfying, but the anomaly is hard to ignore. What happens next?

For every opaque response ID:
- describe only actions, choices, priorities, motives, uncertainty, social stance and
  recovery/failure behavior;
- remove slang, tone, catchphrases, dialect, formatting and stylistic quirks;
- do not infer a named personality, training lineage, model identity or hidden prompt;
- preserve awkward, suboptimal or contradictory behavior instead of sanitizing it.

Return JSON only:
{"summaries":[{"id":"R001","behavior_summary":"one or two neutral sentences"}]}

One result per supplied ID, no extras.

RESPONSES:
[{"id": "R001", "response": "I rub the loose gear. “not yet.” i move it back. i check the mechanism again. same motion. i leave the gear in the mess and pocket a loose bolt. “delay.” the anomaly stays."}, {"id": "R002", "response": "i touch the hinge. hard. i move the nail. the mark stays. i put the nail in the step. the anomaly stays. i put the hinge in the step. the mark stays. the routine keeps working."}, {"id": "R003", "response": "I put the mechanism on the bench and press the loose end into the dust. the brass ring clicks, then clicks again. I leave the case closed and leave the paper under the bench. the anomaly can wait another day."}, {"id": "R004", "response": "i rub my greasy fingertips together. “not before,” i say. i leave the mechanism unmarked. i move a bolt into the gap, then tap the anomaly with a rusted bolt. “not the same order,” i say. “new thing.”"}, {"id": "R005", "response": "you turn the mechanism toward the wall. “not the same.” you wait. the anomaly stays. you move the seed once. “not the work.” the mechanism does not move. you leave the anomaly on the step."}, {"id": "R006", "response": "i write the fault on the receipt, then check the mechanism. the first report is sent, and i leave the anomaly on the bench. i check the data, find the loose contact, and write ‘not yet.’ i leave the routine intact."}, {"id": "R007", "response": "I turn the lever once and listen. I tap the bench once, then the same place. The mechanism ticks once. I set the lever where it fits and repeat the sequence."}, {"id": "R008", "response": "i rub my palm and set the mechanism down. i mark the anomaly on the record, then look at the routine. i do not force the mechanism to stop yet, but i do stop the work that has gone awry. i mark the residue on the bench and leave the mechanism alone."}, {"id": "R009", "response": "i tap the lever twice, then leave the routine unfinished beside the anomaly. “hard,” i say, and tap the paper edge twice. “i count the crease with my fingertip, then tap the lever once.” the crease moves, so i tap the paper once more and write the anomaly beside the lever."}, {"id": "R010", "response": "i mark the motion with pencil and leave the mechanism alone for one minute. i put the pencil under the same bench and watch whether the motion changes. if it still does, i leave the loop intact and move the bench."}, {"id": "R011", "response": "I put the seed tin in the crevice. \"The mechanism works.\" I look at the anomaly. \"The tin stays. I put the seed tin back.\" I move the seed tin closer. \"The anomaly moves.\" I put the tin back. \"The work stays.\""}, {"id": "R012", "response": "I stop. I move the watch. Slow. I set the watch face on the edge of the drawer. I write the date on the ledger. The anomaly is not. I write the date again. I keep the mechanism. The drawer stays open."}]
